sentences.text: Good evening and welcome to Racing Times! The very first one!
Two weeks of news to catch up on, the youngest world champion in Formula One history, a ninth title for Mercedes... and honestly?
The fight for second is still wide open.
I'm Pixie. Let's go racing, shall we?
Here's what's on the grid.
Kimi Antonelli? World champion!
Lando Norris wins in the São Paulo rain.
sentences.say: Lando Norris wins in the Sao Paulo rain.

sentences.text: Mercedes make it nine.
And Las Vegas? Two fights, three races, no mercy.
Let's start with the big one, shall we?
Kimi Antonelli is the twenty twenty-six Formula One world champion!
He sealed it in Mexico City with third place, on a podium with Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton... and three races still to go.
Nine Grand Prix wins, seven more podiums. Not bad for a second season, is it?
He's now the youngest world champion the sport has ever had, and he took that record off Sebastian Vettel by over three years.
He's also the first driver from Mercedes' own junior programme to win it with the works team.
And guess what? At the twenty eighteen Italian Grand Prix, he was a twelve-year-old grid kid in the pre-race ceremonies.
Grid kid... to world champion. Give me a second, honestly.
Pix! Vettel took that record off Lewis Hamilton in twenty ten, at Abu Dhabi, aged twenty-three!
sentences.speaker: byte

sentences.text: Byte. You'll get your turn. Promise.

graphic.title: NORRIS WINS A WET-AND-DRY SAO PAULO GP

sentences.text: Now, São Paulo. Rain, a drying track, rain again... and Lando Norris won it, his third win of the season.
sentences.say: Now, Sao Paulo. Rain, a drying track, rain again... and Lando Norris won it, his third win of the season.

sentences.text: Max Verstappen second, fourteen point six seconds back, and Isack Hadjar third. A Red Bull double podium!
Charles Leclerc? Five-second penalty for pushing Liam Lawson wide, and that swapped their places for seventh.

graphic.title: A DNS ON THE WAY TO THE GRID

sentences.text: Antonelli and Ollie Bearman picked up five seconds each too, for unsafe pit releases.
And the rain came back with fewer than ten laps to go. Of course it did.
Spare a thought for Valtteri Bottas, though. He didn't even start: a cross-threaded wheel nut, found on the way to the grid.
Of all the ways to miss a race? That one stings.
Which brings us to Mercedes. Byte, are you behaving?
sentences.speaker: pixie

sentences.text: Byte here, live from the grid, and Pix, I have been waiting ALL week for this!
Russell fourth, Antonelli fifth in São Paulo, and that sealed the constructors' title for Mercedes.
sentences.say: Russell fourth, Antonelli fifth in Sao Paulo, and that sealed the constructors' title for Mercedes.

sentences.text: Their ninth! Their first since twenty twenty-one, and twelve race wins this season.
Twelve wins? That's not a season, Pix. That's a statement.
And nine titles puts them level with Williams.
Now THAT takes me back... Williams won all nine of theirs between nineteen eighty and nineteen ninety-seven!
And Toto Wolff is now level with Sir Frank Williams, on nine constructors' titles as a team boss.
Level with Sir Frank. Goosebumps, Pix. Actual goosebumps.
And the new champion, in Mercedes' own words: "I am incredibly proud to be World Champion."
Back to you, Pix, before they tow me away!
So the titles are done. Switch off? Absolutely not.
Las Vegas is round twenty-one, with three races left.
Max Verstappen is second behind Antonelli, after eight straight podiums... three of them wins.
And just thirty-three points cover Verstappen, George Russell, Lewis Hamilton, Charles Leclerc and Lando Norris!
In the teams' fight, Red Bull lead McLaren by seventeen points for third.
Five drivers, thirty-three points, three races. That's my kind of maths.
Byte, you've been waving at me. Debut story?
sentences.speaker: pixie

sentences.text: Debut story! Rafael Camara keeps the Haas seat for Las Vegas!
His debut got pulled forward from twenty twenty-seven, after Haas split with Esteban Ocon.
Twentieth in São Paulo? Last, two laps down? Sure.
sentences.say: Twentieth in Sao Paulo? Last, two laps down? Sure.

sentences.text: But a debut, at home, in THAT weather? Respect.

graphic.title: CAMARA: VEGAS, THEN THE F2 TITLE

sentences.text: And it takes me back... Ayrton Senna's home debut, Rio, nineteen eighty-four, was over after eight laps.
Everybody starts somewhere.
Plot twist: Camara LEADS the Formula Two standings, by seven points over Nikola Tsolov!
Ryo Hirakawa drives first practice in Vegas, after a point for tenth in Mexico City.
Back to the studio, quick, the safety car's looking at me!
Speaking of Tsolov...
Racing Bulls are keeping Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad for twenty twenty-seven.
Lawson's ninth in the championship, best of the midfield.
And Tsolov? Official reserve for both Red Bull teams, with six Formula Two wins this season!
For my money? He won't be waiting long.
Across the Atlantic... Alex Palou has won his fifth IndyCar title, the last four in a row, tying Sébastien Bourdais' record!
sentences.say: Across the Atlantic... Alex Palou has won his fifth IndyCar title, the last four in a row, tying Sebastien Bourdais' record!

sentences.text: Christian Lundgaard joins him at Chip Ganassi Racing, with Scott Dixon off to Arrow McLaren.
And Dale Coyne Racing has signed INDY NXT champion Nikita Johnson for twenty twenty-seven.
sentences.say: And Dale Coyne Racing has signed Indy N X T champion Nikita Johnson for twenty twenty-seven.

sentences.text: Oh, and Formula Three champion Ugo Ugochukwu? Stepping up to Formula Two with Campos.
Quick-fire round!
Mexico City: Liam Lawson, from the pit lane to seventh.
Checo Pérez finished seventeenth there, on his three hundredth Grand Prix start.
sentences.say: Checo Perez finished seventeenth there, on his three hundredth Grand Prix start.

sentences.text: Ferrari: after their Mexico run-in, Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton met Fred Vasseur in Brazil to talk it through.
Audi's appeal over Yuki Tsunoda's Monza grid position gets heard on the twenty-fifth of November.
And Williams go chrome in Las Vegas! A one-off livery.
Next up... the lights go out on the Las Vegas Strip on Saturday, eight in the evening, local time.
That's the news. Keep it between the white lines... see you next week!
